properties.name: reflow2's own design always trails what reflow2 can catch — and that lag is the mechanism, not a failure
properties.statement:
A TOOL CAN ONLY CATCH WHAT IT HAS ALREADY BEEN TAUGHT TO CATCH. So reflow2's own design will always contain the class of defect reflow2 is about to learn to detect, and the implementation will always sit behind the detector it is growing. That is the definition of self-hosting, not evidence that anything is wrong.

Anthony, 2026-08-11, in his own words: "we are designing reflow2 using reflow2, so there is always a lag in implementation behind what reflow2 would catch."

WHAT THE RULE ACTUALLY BINDS, which is REPORTING rather than building. A finding of the shape "reflow2 did not catch X in its own design" is not an indictment and must not be written as one. The accurate reading is "X is now catchable, for everyone". Both sentences describe the same measurement; only the second is true about the situation. An agent that writes the first teaches the next reader that the project is failing at the exact moment it is working.

⭐ THE LAG IS THE MECHANISM, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING. Every defect reflow2 finds in its own design is one CONSUMERS WERE ALREADY EXPOSED TO and could not see. The stranded-server defect fixed on 2026-08-11 had hit two other projects before it reached the maintainer, and was reported independently by a third the same week. reflow2's own design is the canary: it is the first place a missing detector shows up as pain, because it is the design under the closest observation. That is why `rule:fixes-are-judged-by-the-third-party` works in practice rather than only in principle — the self-host generates the finding, and the third party is who the fix is FOR.

HIS SECOND HALF, recorded because it is the reason the arrangement is worth its cost: "the kind of cool thing is that because we are using reflow2 to develop itself, we get to see first hand how the things we develop/implement actually work immediately on reflow2 itself - kind of like an immediate feedback."

MEASURED THE SAME DAY, and the shape of the evidence matters. `cap:search-first-at-the-tool` shipped with seven purpose-built tests, all passing and mutation-checked three ways. Within minutes CI surfaced a false-positive class NONE of them held: two requirements with three-word statements refused as near-duplicates, found by an unrelated suite exercising a REAL usage pattern. The synthetic cases came from what an author imagined; the correction came from actual use. A test suite structurally cannot supply that, and the self-host does it for free and immediately.

WHAT THIS RULE DOES NOT LICENCE. It is not an excuse for a defect that was already detectable and was missed — those are ordinary misses and the graph should say so plainly. The lag it forgives is specifically the one between a detector EXISTING and the design it was built from being clean. Nor does it license fixing things here and calling them shipped: `rule:fixes-are-judged-by-the-third-party` still governs, and its named failure — patch it here, mark the requirement met, leave every consumer with the hole — is unaffected by this rule and is the more common error of the two.

ENFORCEMENT: NOT STATED. `DesignRule.enforced` is genuinely three-state and absent means nobody has said, which is the honest record here — Anthony has not been asked whether breaking this should stop a build, and it is a rule about how to READ a finding, so no detector could evaluate it. Asking the consequence question is `cap:governance-proposal`'s job and has not been done for this rule.
